label: Tree Services
audienceNote: Homeowners with a storm-damaged, overgrown or risky tree, and property managers planning routine work. They want a safe, professional crew, a clear quote and proof of past work.
tone: Capable, safety-minded and down to earth. Plain language about the work. No exaggeration.

pages.name: Home
sections: Header with the business name, a click-to-call phone button and a Request a Quote button
Hero: the main service, the service area if known, one primary quote button and one call button
Services overview: tree removal, trimming and pruning, stump grinding, storm clean-up, only those the business actually offers
How it works: request, site assessment and quote, scheduled work (no promised times or prices)
Project gallery section with clearly marked photo placeholders
Questions customers ask (generic, no invented policies)
Final call to action with the phone number and quote request

pages.name: Services
sections: One block per service the business offers, each with a short description and a quote button
Routine work versus urgent or storm work, described without promising response times

pages.name: Contact
sections: Phone, email and address only if provided in the facts; otherwise clearly marked placeholders
Quote request form (preview only: the form must not submit anywhere)
Service area and hours only if provided

trustCueRule: Licensing, insurance, certifications (for example an arborist certification), warranties, years in business, ratings and guarantees may be shown ONLY if they appear in the verified facts. Otherwise leave a clearly marked placeholder such as [TO CONFIRM: insurance details].
imageGuidance: Use no stock photographs of other companies. Use simple inline SVG or CSS shapes (a stylised tree, leaves) and marked photo placeholders such as [PHOTO: crew at work].
